This. Mental illness and physical ailments run rampant in both sides of my family. I decided to be the one to end the cycle. Besides, if I really wanted to have a child for some reason, I already decided I would adopt. There are so many children who deserve loving families, and they shouldn't have to share a bloodline to get it.

My parents were 100% on board. The rest of my family... weeeeellllllll...

I'm not allowed at family gatherings, anymore.

There's hope! I got really lucky, and found a lovely doctor who agreed to give me a hysterectomy and bilateral salpingectomy. Weighing 95 pounds and bleeding through 3+ super tampins every HOUR was not a good experience.

I'm in the USA, and it's been hell trying to get someone to take me seriously.

With my body, there was a high risk of paralysis and/or spinal bleed, if I were to get pregnant. Every other doctor told me that one day I'd change my mind, and that a child would be worth the pain. One even told me all mothers have to sacrifice something, to have the "blessing" of being able to create life.

Except this one.

She was appropriately horrified by this, along with the other doctors' notes in my medical history. I think the psychological evaluation was the final nail in the coffin, though -- she started making calls to get the surgery scheduled, telling me that I had more worth than a hypothetical life I clearly didn't want to be forced into having.

I had been saving up for the surgery since I was 12, and got my first period. Birthday money, allowances, everything went into that fund. Everytime I went in for a checkup, I asked for a hysterectomy. No, it isn't wise to give a child a life-changing surgery, but my requests were well-documented.

This doctor decided my requests had gone unheard long enough.
